paper_title: DR-Unet104 for Multimodal MRI brain tumor
core_problem: Accurate lesion segmentation in brain MRIs, specifically for brain tumors (gliomas), which is a challenging task due to high variation in tumor size, shape, position, and inconsistent intensity/contrast across modalities.
methodology_summary: Proposes a 2D deep residual Unet with 104 convolutional layers (DR-Unet104). Enhancements include adding a 'bottleneck' residual block to the Unet encoder and applying dropout (specifically 0.2) after each convolution block stack for regularization.
datasets_eval: Multimodal Brain Tumor Segmentation (BraTS) 2020 Challenge data (validation and testing sets).
empirical_results: On validation data, DR-Unet104 achieved mean dice scores of 0.8862 (whole tumor), 0.6756 (enhancing tumor), and 0.6721 (tumor core). On the challenge's testing data, final mean DSC scores were 0.8673 (whole tumor), 0.7514 (enhancing tumor), and 0.7983 (tumor core). These results showed an improvement over DeepLabV3+ with a ResNet-V2-152 backbone.
explicit_limitations: The method uses only 2D convolutions, which is noted as a limitation compared to 3D architectures, although this also provides the benefit of running on lower power computers.
